title: Vault Secret Lease Expiry Breaks Database Credentials
description:
impactedApplication: All microservices using dynamic database credentials from HashiCorp Vault
rootCause: The Vault lease renewal sidecar container was not restarted after a Kubernetes node drain, leaving services with expired database credentials that could not be refreshed.
mitigation: Restarted Vault agent sidecars across all affected pods, extended default lease TTL from 1h to 8h, and added lease renewal health checks to readiness probes.
accountableParty: Security Engineering
sourceSystem: HashiCorp Vault / Kubernetes
repeatIncident: False
executiveSummary: 14 microservices lost database connectivity simultaneously at 02:00 UTC when their Vault-issued dynamic credentials expired. The outage lasted 35 minutes and affected payment processing, account lookup, and transaction history APIs.
action_taken: Detection & Triage: Database connection error alerts fired across 14 services at 02:00 UTC. All errors pointed to authentication failures against PostgreSQL. Investigation revealed that Vault dynamic credentials had expired and the renewal sidecar was not running. Engineers restarted the sidecar injectors and forced credential renewal. All services recovered by 02:35 UTC. Post-incident, lease renewal was added as a Kubernetes readiness probe check, ensuring pods are marked unhealthy if credential renewal fails.
root_cause: Vault agent sidecar not restarted after node drain

title: Prometheus TSDB Compaction Failure Causes Monitoring Gap
description:
impactedApplication: Centralized Monitoring Stack (Prometheus + Thanos)
rootCause: A corrupted WAL (Write-Ahead Log) segment prevented TSDB compaction from completing. The head block grew unbounded until Prometheus OOMed at 32GB, causing a 20-minute monitoring blackout.
mitigation: Deleted the corrupted WAL segment, restarted Prometheus with a clean TSDB repair, and configured WAL corruption detection with automatic segment truncation.
accountableParty: Observability Team
sourceSystem: Prometheus / Thanos
repeatIncident: False
executiveSummary: The primary Prometheus instance crashed at 14:22 UTC due to an out-of-memory condition. All metric collection, alerting, and dashboard rendering was unavailable for 20 minutes until a standby instance was promoted.
action_taken: Detection & Triage: Alertmanager went silent at 14:22 UTC (a meta-alert from Thanos querier detected the gap). The standby Prometheus was promoted at 14:30 UTC, restoring alerting. Post-recovery analysis showed the WAL had a corrupted segment from a previous unclean shutdown. TSDB compaction retried against the corrupt segment in a loop, consuming memory until OOM. Engineers repaired the TSDB, deleted the corrupt WAL segment, and restarted. The team implemented WAL integrity checks on startup and automatic segment skip-on-corruption to prevent future OOM spirals.
root_cause: Corrupted WAL segment caused unbounded TSDB head block growth

title: Circuit Breaker Stuck Open on Payment Authorization Service
description:
impactedApplication: Payment Authorization Gateway
rootCause: The circuit breaker library (Resilience4j) had a bug where the half-open state transition timer was not reset after a successful probe, keeping the circuit permanently open after an initial transient failure.
mitigation: Upgraded Resilience4j from 1.7.1 to 2.2.0 which fixed the half-open timer bug, added circuit breaker state monitoring to Grafana, and implemented a manual circuit breaker reset API endpoint for emergency use.
accountableParty: Payment Platform Team
sourceSystem: Payment Authorization Gateway / Resilience4j
repeatIncident: False
executiveSummary: The payment authorization service rejected all incoming requests for 45 minutes starting at 10:15 UTC because the circuit breaker was stuck in the OPEN state. 52,000 payment attempts failed with 'service unavailable' errors despite the downstream issuer service being fully healthy.
action_taken: Detection & Triage: Payment decline rate alerts triggered at 10:18 UTC showing 100% failure rate. Logs showed CircuitBreakerOpenException for all requests. The downstream issuer API was confirmed healthy via direct curl tests. Engineers discovered the circuit breaker was stuck OPEN due to a known bug in Resilience4j 1.7.1 where the half-open timer fails to advance. A rolling restart temporarily fixed it, but the permanent solution was upgrading the library. A manual reset endpoint was also added for future emergencies.
root_cause: Resilience4j bug prevented half-open state transition
